ev.q: In 2022, 7.1% of children and adolescents aged 5–17 years had been the victim of violence or witnessed violence in their neighborhood.

In 2022, 7.1% of children and adolescents aged 5–17 years had been the victim of violence or witnessed violence in their neighborhood.
Percentages were higher among children and adolescents with disabilities (13.9%) than children and adolescents without disabilities (6.0%).
This pattern was observed among children and adolescents aged 5–11 years (12.0% versus 4.8%) and those aged 12–17 years (15.6% versus 7.5%).

equity.level_reason: Percentages are reported by disability status (and age) and described as higher, but the contrast is shown only as side-by-side values with significance statements, with no computed difference or ratio and no disparity framing, so level is capped at 2.

level_alternative.reason: Neighborhood violence is a social determinant outcome, and the higher percentage among children with disabilities (13.9% vs 6.0%) could be read as a quantified contrast.

equity.equity_measurement: Disability is defined from 13 core functioning domains (Child Functioning Questions); the referent is children without disabilities; disability and age are compared as separate margins (2 × 2).

notes: NHIS survey weighting is not stated, so it is not recorded as a procedure. Disability is treated as an SPD because it is the report's primary comparison variable, though it is defined by functional domains.
